**Meridian Tidal Pilot - Final Operations Review Summary**

The primary equipment failure was **Turbine T-4**, which went offline on 14 March 2025 after seawater entered the nacelle through a corroded bearing seal. The root cause was traced to corrosion of the bearing seal housing, causing a multi-week outage—the only such failure in the pilot.

Over the 24-month operating period, the pilot delivered **18.7 GWh** to the grid, which was 6% below the original forecast of 19.9 GWh.

Financially, the project cost **EUR 41.25 million against an approved budget of EUR 36.7 million**, resulting in a **12.4% overrun (EUR 4.55 million)** driven mainly by the T-4 repair campaign.

Environmentally, an independent fish-monitoring programme found **no statistically significant change** in marine migration counts before and after installation (p = 0.41).

Lead engineer Dr. Ines Marchetti recommended replacing the titanium fastener set with duplex stainless steel on all remaining nacelles—a change the steering group accepted in principle.

**Final decision:** The steering group **approved Phase 2 for Q3 2026**, contingent on a completed bearing seal redesign and a successful dry-dock endurance test.
